newsitem.title: MEXICO: Telmex, Alestra head-to-head in long-distance poll.
newsitem.headline: Telmex, Alestra head-to-head in long-distance poll.

text.p: Former Mexican telephone monopoly Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) and the AT&T -backed Alestra were far ahead of their rivals in balloting for long-distance carriers in the northern city of Monterrey, the National Telecommunications Commission (Cofetel) said.

Some 165,636 owners of telephone lines in Monterrey had returned ballots as of January 27 that would allow them to subscribe to a long-distance carrier, according to a Cofetel statement. There are about 522,000 telephone lines in the city, Cofetel said. Final figures for the city are expected within the next few weeks, a Cofetel spokeswoman told Reuters.
Alestra, a joint venture between AT&T, Mexican industrial firm Alfa and holding group VISA-Bancomer, has won 70,236 of the votes, about 42.4 percent of the total.
Telmex, which lost its monopoly on residential service beginning on January 1, garnered 70,144 ballots cast, some 42.3 percent of the total, according to Cofetel.
Avantel, a joint venture between MCI Communications and Mexico's financial group Banamex-Accival, was in a distant third place with 23,620 votes, some 14.2 percent of the poll.
